questions.prompt: For a \(2\times 2\) matrix A, what does A being invertible imply about the equation \(Ax=b\) for every b in \(\mathbb R^2\)?
questions.answer: If A is invertible, then \(Ax=b\) has the unique solution x = \(A^{-1}\)b for every b in \(\mathbb R^2\). Existence follows because \(A^{-1}\)b gives a solution. Uniqueness follows because an inverse cannot send two different inputs to the same output.

questions.prompt: If the RREF of a \(3\times 3\) matrix A is \(I_3\), what can you conclude about A?
questions.answer: If the RREF of A is \(I_3\), then A has a pivot in every column and every row. By the invertible matrix theorem, A is invertible. Therefore \(Ax=b\) has a unique solution for every b in \(\mathbb R^3\), and \(Ax=0\) has only the trivial solution.

questions.prompt: If a \(4\times 4\) matrix A has a zero row in echelon form, what can you conclude about invertibility?
questions.answer: A zero row in echelon form means there is not a pivot in every row. For a square \(4\times 4\) matrix, this also means there is not a pivot in every column. By the invertible matrix theorem, A is not invertible.

questions.prompt: Use the invertible matrix theorem to decide whether A is invertible if \(Ax=0\) has a non-zero solution.
questions.answer: If \(Ax=0\) has a non-zero solution, then the homogeneous system has more than the trivial solution. By the invertible matrix theorem, a square matrix is invertible exactly when \(Ax=0\) has only the trivial solution. Therefore A is not invertible.

questions.prompt: A \(3\times 3\) matrix has pivot columns 1, 2, and 3. What does the invertible matrix theorem imply?
questions.answer: A \(3\times 3\) matrix with pivot columns 1, 2, and 3 has a pivot in every column. Since it is square, it also has a pivot in every row. By the invertible matrix theorem, the matrix is invertible, its columns span \(\mathbb R^3\), and \(Ax=b\) has a unique solution for every b in \(\mathbb R^3\).

questions.prompt: Can a \(3\times 3\) matrix be invertible if its columns do not span \(\mathbb R^3\)? Explain.
questions.answer: No. By the invertible matrix theorem, a \(3\times 3\) matrix is invertible exactly when its columns span \(\mathbb R^3\). If the columns do not span \(\mathbb R^3\), then some vector b in \(\mathbb R^3\) is not reachable as Ax. Therefore \(Ax=b\) fails for that b, and A is not invertible.

questions.prompt: If \(A\) is an invertible \(n\times n\) matrix and \(AB=AC\), prove that \(B=C\).
questions.answer: Since \(A\) is invertible, multiply both sides of \(AB=AC\) on the left by \(A^{-1}\). This gives \(A^{-1}AB=A^{-1}AC\). By associativity, \((A^{-1}A)B=(A^{-1}A)C\). Since \(A^{-1}A=I\), we get \(IB=IC\). Therefore \(B=C\).

questions.prompt: For \(A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&4\end{pmatrix}\), use the homogeneous equation \(Ax=0\) to decide invertibility.
questions.answer: The equation \(Ax=0\) is x + 2y = 0 and 2x + 4y = 0. The second equation is twice the first, so there are non-zero solutions. Let \(y=1\), then \(x=-2\), giving the non-zero solution \((-2, 1)\). Since \(Ax=0\) has a non-zero solution, A is not invertible.

questions.prompt: A square matrix A has RREF \(\begin{pmatrix}1&0&2\\0&1&-1\\0&0&0\end{pmatrix}\). Use the invertible matrix theorem to classify A.
questions.answer: The RREF has a zero row and no pivot in column 3. Therefore A does not have a pivot in every column. By the invertible matrix theorem, A is not invertible. Also, \(Ax=0\) has a free variable and hence has non-zero solutions.

questions.prompt: A learner says a matrix is invertible if \(Ax=b\) has at least one solution for one particular b. Diagnose the error.
questions.answer: Having a solution for one particular b is not enough. The invertible matrix theorem requires \(Ax=b\) to have a unique solution for every b in the codomain. For example, a non-invertible matrix can still satisfy \(Ax=0\) because every homogeneous system has at least the zero solution. Therefore one solvable right side does not prove invertibility.
